title: Jerusalem at the Time of the United Monarchy: The Archaeological Evidence, in Jerusalem in Bible and Archaeology: The First Temple Period
author: Jane M. Cahill
publisher: Society of Biblical Literature (ed. Andrew G. Vaughn and Ann E. Killebrew), pp. 13-80
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted edited-volume chapter. Project stores its own summary of the argument only; no reproduction of the chapter's text, plans, or photographs.
summary: A synthesis defending the maximalist/traditional reading of 10th-century BCE Jerusalem as a genuine fortified town, marshaling the Stepped Stone Structure (excavated in stages by Macalister in the 1920s, Kenyon in the 1960s, and Shiloh's Area G project of 1978-1985) as evidence of substantial Iron I-IIA construction on the City of David ridge, and reading the accumulated ceramic and stratigraphic evidence from these campaigns as consistent with a functioning Israelite capital in David and Solomon's time rather than a negligible hamlet. This project cites Cahill as the named, checkable maximalist counterpart to Steiner (steiner-2003-kenyon-response) and to the Finkelstein-aligned minimalist position, all three published in dialogue with one another in the same edited volume.
